key_insight: A flame-sprayed Fe-based coating achieves its best tribological balance when wear-resistant NiCr-Cr3C2 and lubricating Ni-MoS2 are combined, with the C6 composition delivering the lowest friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: This work offers a practical composition guide for extending service life in sliding components that need both low cost and improved wear resistance.
method: Fe60 was used as the matrix and blended with NiCr-Cr3C2 plus Ni-coated MoS2.
Nine coating formulations were fabricated by flame spraying and compared.
Microstructure, phases, hardness, friction, wear rate, and worn-surface morphology were analyzed.
evidence_signal: Among the nine formulations, C6 (15 wt.% Ni-MoS2 + 40 wt.% NiCr-Cr3C2) showed the lowest friction coefficient (0.50), the lowest wear rate (0.59 × 10^-4 mm3/(N·m)), and the highest microhardness.
watch_item: MoS2 undergoes substantial thermal transformation during spraying, so phase stability and reproducibility under different spray conditions should be carefully controlled.
paper_title: Tribological Properties of Flame-Sprayed Fe-Based Composite Coatings Synergistically Enhanced by NiCr-Cr3C2 and Ni-MoS2
